correctness.rationale: There are 30 normalized Hermitian vectors of support two and 135 of support four, giving 165 points. The tangent hyperplane section at any such point is a cone over a smooth Hermitian plane cubic, and different vertices cannot share more than one line. In a Hermitian frame around an incident line, linearizing the cubic on nearby lines gives two free first-order parameters; requiring the line to continue passing through a given point imposes a linear form whose projective coefficients are that point. Distinct points thus give transverse intersection, so the off-diagonal intersection is one or zero as claimed. Adjunction gives square −3 since K_S is the Plücker class and the genus-one plane cubic has degree three. For the incidence computation, the orthogonal quotient at a point is a three-dimensional nondegenerate Hermitian space with nine isotropic points, giving 36 neighbours. Orthogonal complements of the span of two distinct points have respectively a two-dimensional radical (adjacent) or are nondegenerate of dimension three (nonadjacent), giving 3 or 9 common neighbours. The resulting identity A²=27I−6A+9J, with trace A=0, gives 36,3,−9 of multiplicities 1,120,44; subtracting 3 gives the stated characteristic polynomial. Rank 45 and b2=45 give rational Néron–Severi spanning by the divisor class map. The arithmetic projector at eigenvalue −9 gives trace (15·15−5·30+165)/60=4 and fixed span of dimension 25 including the trivial summand. An independent finite-field enumeration checked all graph and conjugation counts; it does not substitute for the intersection proof.
residual_risks: The formal statement is rational NS spanning only, notwithstanding the broader title. Integral generation, index, discriminant or Picard-scheme assertions are not verified here.

evidence: Cheng's general q-bic results include the Fermat threefold at q=2 in characteristic two. The later Theorem B on the Picard scheme is not itself NS spanning; the earlier intersection lemma is the decisive result. Cor. 4.13 gives 25 over F_p and 45 over F_{p²} for p≡2 mod 3. Roulleau's 30 complex elliptic curves are a different configuration.

originality.rationale: Cheng's prior incidence-divisor lemma explicitly gives the geometric intersection rule for these very divisors, not merely their existence. Specializing to a cubic threefold and q=2 gives A−3I directly; its spectrum follows mechanically from the standard Hermitian point-graph parameters. Rank saturation is then an immediate combination with the published Picard rank and b2 bound, not a new generator theorem. The literal 165-curve spectrum and spanning package need not be printed as a named prior theorem for this coverage to hold.
residual_risks: An explicit printed spectrum or spanning statement might also exist; the verified prior implication is already decisive without it.

value.rationale: The configuration is natural and this is a useful exposition of it. As a distinct finding, however, the proposed geometric invariant is already given by a general rule on the same divisors; the spectrum is a routine strongly regular graph deduction and the span dimension just saturates a published rank. The frozen scope leaves no independently useful unknown exact invariant or new structural consequence, for example an integral index computation, that could carry a repair.
residual_risks: This decision does not judge the value of the underlying prior results or of a genuinely new integral computation, which is not part of the frozen claim.
